reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its compatible norm and Borel measurable structure. Let P be a probability measure on E x R whose first-coordinate marginal is the standard Gaussian measure on E. Here standard Gaussian means the pushforward of independent centered variance-one real Gaussians along (xi_j)_j -> sum_j xi_j e_j for the indicated orthonormal basis of E. There is no positive-dimension assumption. Let p be any real polynomial, and assume that the second-coordinate function ell(x,y)=y belongs to L2(P). No independence between the two coordinates, or Gaussian distribution for the second coordinate, is assumed.

Set S={w in E: ||w||=1}, equipped with its inherited measurable structure. Define the real functions
 f_w(x,y)=p(<w,x>),
 df_{w,v}(x,y)=p'(<w,x>)<v,x>,
where p' is the ordinary polynomial derivative and the inner product is the real ambient inner product. For any measure rho on S define the pointwise scalar predictor
 q_rho(x)=int_S p(<w,x>) d rho(w)
and the scalar ambient potential
 V_rho(w)=2 int_(E x R) (q_rho(x)-y)p(<w,x>) dP(x,y).

The theorem asserts the existence of proofs that f_w is in L2(P) for every w in E and df_{w,v} is in L2(P) for every w,v in E, together with a map D:E -> (E ->L_R L2(P)) and strictly positive real constants M1,M2. Use those integrability proofs to define
 F(w)=[f_w] in L2(P), label=[ell] in L2(P),
 K(w)=F(w) for w in S, and m_rho=int_S K(w) d rho(w).
The last integral is the Bochner integral with values in the real Hilbert space L2(P). Square brackets mean the P-almost-everywhere equivalence class supplied by MemLp.toLp, not equality of arbitrary pointwise representatives.

These witnesses satisfy all of the following:
(1) For every w,v in E, D(w)(v)=[df_{w,v}] in L2(P).
(2) For every w in E, F has real Frechet derivative D(w) at w. Equivalently, F(w+h)-F(w)-D(w)(h) is o(||h||) in the L2 norm as h tends to zero.
(3) For every w with ||w||<=1, the operator norm satisfies ||D(w)||<=M1.
(4) For every w,u with ||w||<=1 and ||u||<=1, ||D(w)-D(u)||<=M2||w-u||, using the operator norm on maps E -> L2(P).

Furthermore, for every probability measure rho on S, all the following conclusions hold together:
(a) For every x in E, the scalar function w -> p(<w,x>) is rho-integrable. This is an every-x statement, not merely a Gaussian-almost-everywhere statement.
(b) K:S -> L2(P) is Bochner integrable with respect to rho.
(c) The function (x,y) -> q_rho(x) belongs to L2(P), and its L2 equivalence class equals m_rho:
 [q_rho composed with the first projection]=m_rho.
(d) As functions on all of E,
 V_rho(w)=2 <m_rho-label,F(w)>_(L2(P)).
The L2 inner product is the integral of the pointwise product of representatives; its value is independent of their P-null-set choices.
(e) For every w in E, the function (x,y) -> (q_rho(x)-y)p(<w,x>) is P-integrable, and V_rho has ambient Hilbert-space gradient
 2 D(w)^*(m_rho-label)
at w. In particular its actual ambient gradient satisfies
 grad V_rho(w)=2 D(w)^*(m_rho-label).
The star denotes the continuous-linear-map Hilbert adjoint, characterized by
 <v,D(w)^* r>_E=<D(w)v,r>_(L2(P)).
The statement includes both the HasGradientAt assertion and the equality for the defined gradient function.
(f) Define on E the ambient vector field
 G_rho(w)=grad V_rho(w)-<grad V_rho(w),w>_E w.
For every unit vector w in S, the following vector equality in E holds:
 G_rho(w)=2 [D(w)^*(m_rho-label)-<D(w)^*(m_rho-label),w>_E w].
For unit w this is the orthogonal projection of the ambient gradient onto w-perpendicular. The displayed definition and identity do not assert an identification with an additional intrinsic-manifold or measure-space differential API.

D,M1,M2 and the feature/derivative integrability witnesses are selected before rho is quantified, so the same witnesses and constants work for every probability measure rho on S. The statement gives no formulas for M1,M2 and makes no uniformity claim as E,P or p vary; the witnesses may depend on those preceding data. The constants do not depend on rho,w,u or v. Differentiability and the ambient-gradient assertions are global in w, whereas the norm and Lipschitz estimates for D are restricted to the closed unit ball. No numerical bound or Lipschitz estimate for G_rho, and no gradient-flow, transport or evolution conclusion, is part of the proposition. If E has dimension zero, the unit sphere may be empty; no probability measure on it is presumed to exist.
objects: Finite-dimensional real inner-product space E with Borel sigma-algebra; probability law P on E x R with standard-Gaussian first marginal and square-integrable second coordinate; arbitrary real polynomial p; unit sphere S; scalar features f_w and directional feature derivatives df_{w,v}; L2 classes F, label and K; Bochner feature mean m_rho; scalar predictor q_rho and potential V_rho; continuous-linear derivative D(w), its Hilbert adjoint, positive constants M1,M2 and projected ambient gradient field G_rho.
domains: E is arbitrary finite-dimensional real inner-product space, including dimension zero. P is on E x R. S is the norm-one subtype of E with inherited measurable structure; rho ranges over all probability measures on S. w,u,v,x range over all E unless a closed-unit-ball or sphere condition is explicitly stated. Features and predictors are real-valued functions on E x R; F and m_rho lie in the real Hilbert space L2(P). D(w):E ->L_R L2(P), and D(w)^*:L2(P) ->L_R E. There is no time parameter.
quantifiers: For every eligible E and its structures and every P with probability mass one and first marginal stdGaussian E, for every real polynomial p and proof that the second coordinate is in L2(P), there exist hf for all w, hdf for all w,v, one D and M1,M2>0. Their derivative formula and global differentiability hold for all ambient w,v; bounds hold for all w,u in the closed unit ball. Only then, for every rho that is a probability measure on S, all scalar/Bochner integrability, L2 predictor identification, potential/gradient identities and the all-unit-w projection identity hold. The predictor L2 proof witness is existential inside the rho conclusion.
assumptions: Compatible real inner-product/normed additive structure on E, finite dimension and its Borel measurable structure; P is a probability measure; map fst P=stdGaussian E; p is a real polynomial; z->z.2 belongs to L2(P). The rho-specific conclusions assume only that rho is a probability measure on the norm-one sphere. Feature/feature-derivative/predictor L2 membership, integrability and differentiability are conclusions, not extra premises. No coordinate independence, Gaussian labels, positive dimension, preselected derivative, tangent hypothesis or supplied regularity bound is assumed.
conclusion: Existence of global L2 feature and directional-derivative classes and D with D(w)v=[p prime(<w,x>)<v,x>]; HasFDerivAt F D(w) at every w; positive operator-norm bound M1 and derivative Lipschitz bound M2 on the closed unit ball. For every sphere probability rho: every-x scalar predictor integrability, Bochner integrability of K, L2 predictor class equal to m_rho, V_rho=2< m_rho-label,F(.) > as functions on E, integrability of its defining scalar product for every w, HasGradientAt and grad V_rho(w)=2D(w)^*(m_rho-label), and the stated orthogonal-projection vector identity for every w in S.
scopes: Global Frechet differentiability and ambient-gradient conclusions at each w; derivative norm/Lipschitz bounds only when the relevant arguments lie in the closed unit ball. Predictor integrability holds for every x, not only almost everywhere. L2 equalities are equalities of P-a.e. classes; they imply only a.e. equalities of selected function representatives. Potential equality is pointwise for all ambient w, and the final projection equality is pointwise on S. No convergence-in-time, flow, transport, intrinsic API identification or bound on G_rho is asserted.
constant_dependencies: M1 and M2 are strictly positive existential real numbers, with no explicit formulas. Their quantifiers precede rho,w,u,v, so they are uniform over all sphere probability measures rho and all points used in the indicated unit-ball bounds. The statement permits dependence on preceding data E,P,p and supplies no uniform choice as those vary. Factors 2 and unit sphere radius 1 are exact. The Gaussian marginal has covariance identity/coordinate variance 1; no additional scale or dimension-dependent numerical formula is stated.

definition_reconstruction.stdGaussian: Pushforward of the product of centered variance-one real Gaussian laws on Fin(finrank_R E) coordinates by the orthonormal-basis synthesis map.
definition_reconstruction.MemLp: Almost-everywhere strong measurability together with finite eLpNorm; at exponent 2 this is square integrability.
definition_reconstruction.Lp_and_toLp: Lp is a subgroup of the almost-everywhere equivalence-class space with finite p-norm. MemLp.toLp constructs the class of the given function; its coerced representative agrees with the original only P-almost everywhere.
definition_reconstruction.predictor: q_rho(x)=integral over the actual unit sphere of p(<w,x>) against rho.
definition_reconstruction.F_label_K_mean: F(w)=[f(w)], label=[(x,y)->y], K=F restricted to S, mean(rho)=the L2-valued Bochner integral of K against rho.
definition_reconstruction.L2_inner: Integral of products of real-valued a.e. representatives, as supplied by L2.inner_def.
definition_reconstruction.Frechet_derivative: Little-o error F(w+h)-F(w)-D(w)h relative to h at w, in the norm topology of L2(P).
definition_reconstruction.gradient: Riesz-inverse of the real Frechet derivative. The theorem explicitly proves HasGradientAt, so the asserted value is a genuine gradient rather than relying on a default outside differentiability.
definition_reconstruction.G: G_rho(w)=grad V_rho(w)-<grad V_rho(w),w>w on E; on the unit sphere it is the orthogonal tangent projection.

representative_boundary: The statement uses genuine L2 equivalence classes via MemLp.toLp and an L2-valued Bochner mean. It identifies the pointwise-defined predictor with that mean as an L2 class; it does not choose a jointly pointwise canonical representative of the entire L2 mean family.
read_scope: Only the designated anonymous decoder-input.json and the result written beside it; no source/module/capsule/review, neighboring directory or implementation was consulted.
